articles.title: COP31 draft 'quite silent' on fossil fuels, as talks close to final deal
articles.summary: Fossil fuels were not explicitly mentioned in the latest draft deal from the Conference of the Parties 31 (COP31) held in Antalya, Türkiye, on Sunday, despite the issue being at the centre of the fractious talks. The revised deal, published late at night at COP31, calls for electrifying the global economy. COP31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia had pitched "electrification" as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security. The proposal includes previous agreement reached in 2023 to shift from oil, gas, and coal but omits mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change. “We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a plenary session early on Sunday. He said the conference would reconvene in the morning to approve the deal. Environmental group 350.org said it was disappointed by the draft's failure to mention fossil fuels explicitly, as well as its encouragement of carbon-removal technologies. COP31 talks drag on as nations remain divided over fossil fuel phase-out Negotiations were extended into 'extra time' on Saturday, as the nations struggled to resolve differences regarding fossil fuel emissions, at the same time considering the Global South’s demand for economic growth. Saudi Arabia, Russia and India are among the countries understood to have opposed any decisive reference to the “phase-out of fossil fuels” in the text. "We are very disappointed with how the text looks," the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told news agency AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency's offices. "I can't honestly say that I'm okay with it passing" in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was "quite silent" on fossil fuels. The draft deal retains a proposal to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 alongside efforts to expand the use of "clean energy" and calls for accelerating carbon capture and storage. Critics said that the electric alternatives should be powered by renewable energy, whereas certain environmental groups expressed disappointment over non-explicit mentioning of fossil fuels, and encouraging carbon capture and storage technologies. (With agency inputs)

articles.title: Puttur medical college: Three-member RGUHS panel inspects sites for new campus
articles.summary: Puttur: A three-member inspection committee from the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) visited Puttur on Saturday to assess the infrastructure and facilities required to establish the proposed government medical college . The team inspected the old court building in Puttur, which is being developed for temporary medical college classrooms, the Government General Hospital, and the site at Bannur earmarked for construction of the medical college building. Other locations identified for supporting facilities were also inspected. The inspection committee was headed by Dr Suresh S Kanakannavar, Senate member of the RGUHS. Its other members were Dr Ramesh Babu, Dean of Shivamogga Institute of Medical Sciences (SIMS), and Dr Mithun K M of Subbaiah Institute of Dental Sciences, Shivamogga. Medical college nodal officer Dr Lohith Kumar, Dr Shashank K J, Assistant Executive Engineer Gurupasad and Puttur Government Hospital Administrative Medical Officer Dr Yaduraj accompanied the team. 111 graduate from Father Muller Medical College in Mangaluru MLA Ashok Rai was also present during the inspection of the old court building, where arrangements are being made to conduct the medical college's initial teaching sessions. Dr Suresh S Kanakannavar said the committee will assess whether the proposed institution had adequate facilities, including classrooms, laboratories, a teaching hospital, hostels, staff accommodation and sufficient land. A detailed report will be prepared and submitted to RGUHS for consideration and approval. Once cleared by the university, the proposal will be forwarded to the National Medical Commission (NMC) in New Delhi for further scrutiny and permission. "If the approval process proceeds smoothly and all necessary infrastructure, buildings and hostel facilities are ready, classes could commence by September 2027," he said. Nodal officer Dr Lohith Kumar said an application had been submitted to RGUHS on October 8 seeking approval to establish the Puttur Medical College and Research Institute for the 2027-28 academic year. MLA Ashok Rai said renovation, painting and other preparatory works were underway, while additional beds were being arranged at the government hospital. Mangaluru: Basel Mission Museum and Art Gallery inauguration on December 2 He added that a proposal for recruiting 97 doctors, 70 nurses and 175 other staff members was currently pending with the state government's Finance Department and that approval was expected shortly. Regarding accommodation for students, Rai said existing government buildings in the area will be utilised to create hostel facilities for 50 students, with arrangements expected to be completed before the college begins functioning. He said the medical college will begin operations in September 2027 using temporary facilities and will subsequently shift to its new permanent campus at Sediyap in its second year.

articles.title: PANI project to connect Andaman's eight islands, provide 4G connectivity to 87 villages
articles.summary: Sri Vijaya Puram: The Centre is considering a series of initiatives to strengthen digital connectivity across the Andaman and Nicobar Islands , including a proposed undersea cable network connecting eight islands and an expansion of 4G mobile services to 87 villages currently without network coverage. The proposals were discussed during a meeting between Union Telecommunications Secretary Amit Agrawal and Andaman and Nicobar Islands Lieutenant Governor Dinesh Sharma, along with senior officials of the Central government and the Andaman and Nicobar Administration, according to a release issued by Lok Niwas here on Saturday. A key focus of the meeting was the proposed PANI (Port Alternative Network for Islands) Project , under which eight islands - Diglipur, Mayabunder, Shaheed Dweep, Chowra, Teressa, Katchal, Nancowry and Little Nicobar - are proposed to be connected through a submarine optical fibre cable network. Centre notifies new prison regulation for Andaman and Nicobar, replacing colonial era laws The project is expected to address mobile and internet connectivity challenges in remote islands and ensure more reliable communication, particularly during emergencies, it said. The proposed network, originating in Puri in Odisha, will also provide an alternative connectivity route to the existing Chennai-Andaman and Nicobar Islands (CANI) submarine cable network. This redundancy is expected to help maintain internet services in the event of disruption or damage to the existing cable system. During the meeting, the Lieutenant Governor suggested including Dugong Creek in the proposed network and establishing a cable landing station there to further expand the network's reach and reliability, the release said. The meeting also reviewed the implementation of the 4G saturation scheme under the Digital Bharat Nidhi. A proposal was discussed to extend 4G mobile connectivity to 87 uncovered villages across the islands, prioritising villages based on their population. The initiative is aimed at bringing residents of remote and inaccessible areas into the mobile network. Another major area of discussion was the acceleration of the revised BharatNet Programme, which aims to provide Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) connectivity to 174 villages that remain uncovered, it said. While 70 gram panchayats have already been covered under the programme, four of the seven tribal council areas have also been connected. Efforts are planned to extend connectivity to the remaining three tribal council areas. Andaman & Nicobar administration seeks suggestions from public for naming 586 uninhabited islands The Lieutenant Governor stressed the need to expedite fibre-network expansion to the remaining uncovered villages to ensure wider access to digital services. The initiatives are aimed at improving access to online services, digital facilities and emergency communication for residents across the geographically dispersed islands, the release added.

articles.title: The Amazon who bought me: How Bezos captured ‘007’, gave Robert Pattinson another iconic role
articles.summary: James Bond was once owned not by Hollywood studios but by a family. For over six decades, the cinematic rights of the world's most famous spy James Bond was with an American film-producing family, Broccoli family. Since 1962, the Broccoli dynasty, which was first led by legendary producer Albert R. "Cubby" Broccoli, and later by his children Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, guarded '007' with an uncompromising devotion, through their holding company Danjaq, which was formed in alliance with Harry Saltzman to control Bond's rights. And over the years, the Broccoli family kept these rights of James Bond on a tight leash. From deciding which actor will be donning the ultra famous secret agent's tuxedo and gun to giving their final nod to every director and script, it was always the family whose last word that mattered. In 1965, Saltzman decided to sell his 50 per cent stake in Danjaq owing to financial pressures and increasing disputes. In 2022, tech giant Amazon, founded by billionaire Jeff Bezos, closed a massive $8.5 billion acquisition of Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM). By buying the legacy studio from Saltzman, Amazon inherited an exact 50 percent stake in the Bond franchise and its theatrical distribution rights. From Yash & Shah Rukh Khan to Hrithik Roshan: Indian actors we'd love to see as James Bond In a move that sent shockwaves through the entertainment industry, the long-lasting reign of the Broccoli family came to an end in February 2025, when Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson stepped back from their roles as active creative stewards. They formed a historic joint venture with Amazon MGM Studios, officially ceding creative control of the intellectual property to the tech giant in a deal estimated around $1 billion. While the Broccolis remain co-owners of the trademark, the keys to the Aston Martin now officially belong to Amazon. In November 2026, Amazon flexed its new creative muscles, announcing Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond under the direction of Denis Villeneuve. The announcement took the internet by storm as people started to debate the casting of Pattinson, famous for The Twilight Saga and The Batman , and whether his deep, brooding intensity would seamlessly translate into the smooth, lethal sophistication of cinema's greatest secret agent. 'Identity Confirmed': Robert Pattinson announced to play next James Bond Jeff Bezos was heavily involved in casting Robert Pattinson Speaking at an event in California, Bezos shared that he was "heavily involved" in casting the new James Bond and revealed that he was initially sceptical about casting Pattinson as the new James Bond, given his existing stardom and popularity, and this, goes against the rule of casting the secret agent, who for the last 64 years, have been lesser-known actors with an unmatched mystery, whose identities wouldn't overshadow the character of 007. "But there was something special about Rob and his performance. It was immediately undebated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director … we all gravitated toward Rob. Initially, we were slightly biased against him just because he’s already so famous, like maybe we should have somebody more unknown, but in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond," Bezos said at the event, as quoted by Variety. Brad Pitt wants to be signed up for villain as Robert Pattinson gets 'license to kill' as new James Bond Bond through the years All the actors who had played Bond were either unknown, lesser-known actors or TV stars. Here's a list of all the actors who have played James Bond over the years: Sean Connery (1962) George Lazenby (1969) Roger Moore (1973) Timothy Dalton (1987) Pierce Brosnan (1995) Daniel Craig (2005) The most recent movie in James Bond's franchise was No Time to Die (2021) starring Daniel Craig.

The district-level attention to the situation will help facilitate focused implementation and effective monitoring of pollution measures at the grassroots. "Dealing with air pollution requires sustained and concerted efforts based on the airshed approach. For 2027, annual action plans shall also be prepared at the district level, in addition to the state and municipal corporation levels," the CAQM said. The action plan for next year will have defined sector-wise actions with achievable targets, the CAQM order stated, with timelines and monitoring parameters. A focused approach will be in place across the major pollution sources including a list of strong probable's like vehicles, road dust, industrial emissions, construction and demolition drives, solid waste, crop residues, diesel generator sets, crematoria, and other local sources. 50 years of air pollution studies show need for multi-pollutant approach Officials responsible for achieving the prescribed targets will be specifically identified by their names and designations, thereby establishing clear ownership, responsibility and accountability for implementation and outcomes, the CAQM said. "These significant additions to the state action plans are of critical importance in advancing the Commission's mandate of ensuring sustained improvement in air quality and making the air breathable for citizens across Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas," the CAQM said. articles.title: Mangaluru: Basel Mission Museum and Art Gallery inauguration on December 2
articles.summary: Mangaluru: The Basel Mission Museum and Art Gallery at Karnataka Theological College (KTC), Balmatta, will be inaugurated on December 2 by former Union Minister Veerappa Moily. The newly constructed four-floor facility, spanning approximately 20,000 square feet, is an initiative of KTC to preserve and showcase the historical, literary, cultural, and technological contributions of the Basel Mission to Karnataka . Guulshan Roy is the architect of this unique structure. The Basel Mission played a pioneering role in the region's development through its contributions to education, literature, journalism, printing, industry, and social transformation. Mangaluru Police rescue med student 'forcibly taken away by her family' Mangalura Samachara, published by Hermann Moegling, marked a milestone in Kannada journalism. The Basel Mission Press, established in 1841, contributed significantly to printing and publishing, while its tile factory, established in 1860, pioneered tile manufacturing in India and introduced the iconic Mangalore tiles. Rev. Ferdinand Kittel's Kannada Dictionary remains a landmark in Kannada linguistic scholarship. Established by the Basel Mission in 1847, Karnataka Theological College continues to uphold this heritage. Its archives hold a valuable collection of historical documents, rare publications, photographs, and artefacts relating to the history and culture of the region. Although the archives have become an important resource for researchers, limitations of space and facilities, along with restricted public access to much of the collection, prompted the College to establish a dedicated museum and exhibition facility. The museum will feature rare literary works, including the Kittel Kannada Dictionary, Gundert Malayalam Dictionary, Tulu Dictionary, Kannada and Tulu grammar books, classical publications, and Mangaluru Samachara. Historical printing equipment, artefacts associated with the Basel Mission's industrial contributions, and at the later stage more than 5,000 photographs documenting the region's people, institutions, architecture, education, industries, and cultural life will also be displayed. The Art Gallery and exhibition spaces will provide opportunities to engage with the region's artistic and cultural heritage, said a release from KTC Principal Rev Dr H M Watson.

articles.title: I do not shoot arrows from behind, I am straightforward: Keralam minister Muraleedharan
articles.summary: Thiruvananthapuram: Keralam Health Minister K Muraleedharan on Sunday denied allegations that he had leaked details of differences within the state Cabinet, saying he was not someone who "shoots arrows from behind" and believed in straightforward functioning. Responding to reporters' queries here about reports of heated exchanges between Chief Minister V D Satheesan and some of his Cabinet colleagues over the appointment of Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) members, and allegations that Muraleedharan had leaked details of the differences, he said he believed in straightforward functioning. "I do not shoot arrows from behind. I am straightforward in my approach and do not indulge in such indirect attacks," he said. K Muraleedharan backs Keralam CM Satheesan, says govt will complete 5-year term "There is no need for a discussion on this now. Several good things being done by the government have been pushed into the background. Instead of giving importance to such issues, we should focus on the government's projects and ensure that the government moves forward together. That is the decision we have collectively taken," he said. He also denied any lack of coordination within the Congress and the United Democratic Front (UDF). "Otherwise, we would not have won 102 seats. Could the Congress have secured 102 seats if it had remained inactive? The party, the front and the government will continue to move forward together," he said. He said the Cabinet had been meeting every Wednesday since the government assumed office and the chief minister had been briefing the media on Cabinet decisions, reflecting the systematic functioning of the government. Won't let anyone to 'hijack' state govt event: Keralam's Muraleedharan displeased over full rendition of Vande Mataram Differences were natural in democratic movements and could be resolved, he said, adding that the delay in finalising the PSC members' list was not significant. "There was a small doubt raised by the chief minister about one name. It was resolved immediately on the same day, before he left for Delhi the next day. The list has been sent to the Governor. Once the Governor's order comes, the appointments of the four or five members will be notified," he said. He also said the Congress had never received such a large share of PSC members and government pleader positions under the party quota in the past, but only negative issues were being discussed. Asked about his sister Padmaja Venugopal quitting the BJP and returning to the Congress, Muraleedharan said he had already responded to the issue and did not wish to repeat his remarks. Kerala High Court says Guruvayur temple staff must treat devotees with respect, maintain calm "The KPCC president and the CM can decide on such matters. I have already said what I had to say, and there is no need for me to intervene further," he said. On Ambalapuzha independent MLA G Sudhakaran, who was backed by the UDF in the Assembly election, criticising Congress leaders, Muraleedharan described him as an elder statesman whose advice was valued. "He is a senior leader and we are willing to accept his suggestions. He has been making reasonable interventions on issues such as Alappuzha Medical College, and we have implemented several of his suggestions. We will consider his advice with due respect," he said. On a young woman in Malappuram reportedly suffering from a kidney ailment after using a face cream promoted through Instagram, the minister cautioned people against using unapproved products sold online. "People should check where such products are manufactured before applying them to their faces. There are several government-approved creams available. Applying creams does not necessarily enhance beauty. The government will take action based on complaints received," he said. He clarified that such products did not come under the purview of the Food Safety Department as they were not food items. Asked whether regulations would be introduced, he said the government would decide on the matter, which had recently come to its notice. On the online sale of unapproved medicines, Muraleedharan said the government was considering the issue and would soon take a decision. "The government is looking into this even in the absence of a specific complaint. We will not allow such medicines to be sold in this manner. If specific complaints are received about any medicines, action will be taken after examination," he said.

articles.summary: Raja Singh, the controversial MLA from Telangana, has once again made inflammatory comments against Muslims, asking Hindus to keep licensed guns in their homes if India doesn’t bring in population regulation law restricting people from having more than two children. He made the remarks while referring to a recent Pew Research Center study projecting that Muslims’ population share would go up by five percentage points between 2020 and 2070. The video showing him holding a rifle and sitting amidst a group of men in Uttar Pradesh while advocating for ‘gun culture’ among Hindus was shared by the Goshamhal MLA himself, according to ANI. Raja Singh referred to recent news reports on a Pew Research Center study which projected that between 2020 and 2070, Muslims’ population share in India will go up from 15% to 20%, while that of Hindus will decrease from about 79% to 76%. “If their (Muslims’) population share rises, will Hindus be safe?” Raja Singh asked the people gathered around him. Though he resigned from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2025 objecting to the party’s choice in appointing the Telangana party president, he referred to the BJP as “our party”. He said, “In the coming days, while our party and Prime Minister Narendra Modi is in power, if a two-child law is not passed, then every Hindu must start keeping licensed guns at home. If a Hindu doesn’t keep a gun, they will have no property, sister or daughter left,” claiming that there would be a rise in atrocities against Hindus, invoking violence against the Hindu minority in Pakistan. Saying that he liked the “gun culture” in Uttar Pradesh, he added, “I believe every home in Uttar Pradesh has a licensed gun. Similarly, every household in India must have one.” The Pew Research Center study, titled ‘The Future of World Religions: Population Growth Projections, 2020-2070’ released on November 18, projected that despite a dip in Hindus’ population share of three percentage points by 2070, Hindus will maintain their numerical dominance and will continue to comprise more than 75% of the nation’s populace. India’s Hindu population is expected to rise from 1.113 billion to 1.289 billion while the Muslim population will grow from 213 million to nearly 334 million. The changes stem mainly from differences in age and fertility, the study says. The fertility rate for Indian Hindus was estimated at 1.9 children per woman in the 2020–2025 period, while it is 2.3 for per woman for Muslims. While the total fertility rates have been higher among Muslims than Hindus for a few years now, the overall fertility rate as well as that among both Hindus and Muslims have been steadily declining with time, as per the National Family Health Surveys (NFHS) conducted by the Union Health Ministry. While Muslim fertility rate is the highest among all religions as per NFHS-5 (2019-21), the community’s total fertility rate has also seen the sharpest decline by about one percentage point (from 3.4 to 2.4). articles.title: A Duck’s Tale: Arun Varghese on his quirky satire rooted in the backwaters of Kuttanad
articles.summary: Ducks, wobbling about on land and water, are such a common sight in small towns of Kerala, especially in Kuttanad, that you don’t pause to take a second look when you hear their ceaseless quacking. So, when A Duck’s Tale , a Malayalam movie set to premiere at the International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK) next month, begins with a flock of ducks swimming in the night, you don’t think much of it, beyond making a vague connection to the title. But Arun Varghese, who grew up in Kuttanad, manages to pick out a single duck from that flock and weave several stories around it, in his debut film. He has written and directed A Duck’s Tale with the production team that made the critically acclaimed Baakki Vannavar , released two years ago. Salmaanul, who played the quiet protagonist in Baakki Vannavar , turns into an expressive, frustrated young man in A Duck’s Tale , with both films putting him in the garb of an unemployed youth. “Yes, but in this case it is more because he is lazy, not trying hard, while Baakki Vannavar was more about the system,” Arun says in an interview with TNM. Malayalam film Baaki Vannavar explores unemployment through a gig worker's life He too, like the protagonist, is an engineering graduate, and had a stint in the IT sector for a few years before reconnecting with a passion that began in childhood, making films. “It was all short films before, which I mostly wrote for and sometimes directed. It had continued in my IT days in Bengaluru too,” Arun says. Arun Varghese In his first feature film, Arun chooses a few incidents from his childhood, connects them to the ducks he was so used to seeing in his hometown, and looks at serious issues through a lens of humour. Children play a big part in the film, with the whole story set off by a little boy who is upset because he is not offered duck curry at a friend’s home. “That is from my childhood, a story I don’t remember but had heard about. I was the child who was upset at not getting the duck curry,” he says. For the film, he picked children from schools in Kuttanad. They speak the language, know the terrain, and move comfortably across the fields and along the backwaters. One of the child actors in 'A Duck's Tale' Salmaanul shows his range, playing a man going through multiple troubles, including unemployment and relationship issues. He is nothing like the sad gig worker in Baakki Vannavar . Pramod Velliyanad is another versatile actor, playing the overly meddlesome local leader, who is everywhere and wants to stick his nose into everything. Women characters, the mothers and the lover, are thoughtfully written, distinct, and adorably genuine, especially the sister in the family that Pramod visits. The music, by Neeraj Remesh, is also a welcome addition, noticeable as it stretches in a sequence of two boys cycling down a road, talking about their evening game, before one of them continues to walk into a shocking situation. You might spot, if you look for it, a few drawbacks or areas to improve. But it is an admirable debut, original in its theme and treatment, lacking any pretentiousness in becoming an offbeat satire. A Duck’s Tale has been chosen in the Malayalam Cinema category of the IFFK, which begins on December 11.

articles.title: UP Police mistakenly give Owaisi guard of honour meant for Supreme Court judge
articles.summary: In a hilarious goof-up, the police in Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh, mistakenly accorded a guard of honour to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Saturday, November 21, after confusing his convoy with that of a Supreme Court judge expected at the Circuit House. The police contingent had assembled at the government premises to receive the judge when Owaisi arrived with a convoy carrying Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief Chandrashekhar Aazad. As soon as the AIMIM chief arrived at the Circuit House, a group of four police personnel in ceremonial attire stood at the entrance of the building to perform the gun salute. Owaisi stopped and received it before proceeding inside. The mix-up was noticed shortly afterwards and brought to the attention of senior police officials. The judge did not arrive at the Circuit House, an officiating Reserve Inspector told The Indian Express . Owaisi later said he did not know why the salute had been given to him. He said police personnel asked him to stand for the salute and he followed their instructions. Saharanpur Senior Superintendent of Police directed the Superintendent of Police (Rural) to investigate the incident. Police said action would be taken in accordance with the rules based on the facts and evidence gathered during the inquiry. The incident has raised questions about protocol and coordination among personnel deployed at the Circuit House. Owaisi was in Saharanpur with Chandrashekhar Aazad ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The two leaders recently announced the Samajik Parivartan Morcha, a political front expected to contest the polls. Owaisi was also scheduled to meet district officials and attend a joint press conference with Aazad. articles.title: India vs New Zealand | Rishabh Pant smashes century as visitors continue to dominate
articles.summary: Wellington: Playing his first match since being rendered hors de combat after the Irani Cup final that concluded on October 4, maverick Rishabh Pant showed no ring rust whatsoever in crafting a matured century while India obliterated several records as the visitors set themselves up nicely for a famous win over New Zealand in the opening Test here on Sunday. Having already reached the halfway stage of the three-figure milestone on Saturday itself at Basin Reserve, Pant resumed from where he left off, hammering a 153-ball 128 on the fourth day to join team-mate KL Rahul and become the sixth Indian to score a ton in SENA (South Africa, England, New Zealand, Australia) nations. Dhruv Jurel, the reserve wicketkeeper for main man Pant but playing in this game as a pure batter, joined in the run-fest with an equally attractive 79-ball 78 while nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj did his part to perfection with a quickfire 38 in the morning session as India declared at massive 720/9 — the highest team score against the Black Caps and in New Zealand. Leading by 352 runs, India put New Zealand through the wringer on absolute batting paradise that showed no signs of major wear and tear and the hosts managed to stay in the fight after taking stumps at 119/2. While India are still the favourites to nick this game, they’ll be aware of the some missed chances in recent years from such promising positions and they’ll have to be at their best on Monday given how flat the track has remained with no demons in it. India vs New Zealand | K L Rahul 2.0 loading, the man with a mission Earlier, when the day began, it was actually Kamboj the aggressor. He ended up getting most of the strike during the opening half hour and he showed he’s no muck with the bat in carting some punchy boundaries to set up a nice tone for the charge. One, however, can’t keep Pant out of the game for long and the southpaw hit his stride with a boundary and six off Kyle Jamieson off consecutive deliveries in the fifth over of the morning. But after that he tempered down his aggression as New Zealand bowled to a plan. They strengthened the off-side and bowled slightly wide, forcing him to take risks by manufacturing shots on the on-side. Accused — fairly and unfairly — of throwing his wicket away at times, Pant, completely aware that he could join a league of extraordinary gentlemen and bat New Zealand out of the game, showed wonderful restraint. He didn’t fish for anything on the off-side nor did he try to do something unnatural, like a scoop or stepping down. He was happy to soak up all the pressure and defended doughtily. He knew at some stage New Zealand would err and that would be the time to punish them. India vs New Zealand | Defence is the form of attack for Akash Deep It arrived when he was in the 90s, a phase that has often tormented him. Sunday was special though, Pant playing the reverse sweep to kick on to 99 and then dispatching Glenn Phillips’ very next delivery over long-off for a massive six to bring his 9th Test century and place himself into the history books. Once the mission was complete, Pant went hammer and tongs in search of quick runs. Jurel too did the same from the other end before India declared a little before tea. Jasprit Bumrah got India off to the perfect start when he sent back skipper Tom Latham for a second duck of the match. India then dismissed Henry Nicholls after Jurel pulled off a stunning catch at short-leg and tried to rattle Rachin Ravindra (27 n.o.) with Prasidh Krishna giving him some lip service. It was tense but Ravindra and Conway (59 n.o.) survived but the real test of character comes on Monday. articles.title: Karunadotsava | 10 places you must visit in Karnataka
articles.summary: The Stone Chariot in Hampi. Hampi Set against boulder fields and banana groves along the Tungabhadra, Hampi was the heart of the Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century. It features, among others, the carved stone chariot at Vijaya Vittala temple complex and the Virupaksha Temple, with Matanga Hill overlooking the entire area. The Akka-Tangi falls in Badami. Badami Sitting right on the edge of Agastya Lake, Badami has a heavy, ancient history to it. Back when it was called Vatapi, it was the capital of the early Chalukya dynasty. Its incredible rock-cut cave architecture and stone sculptures easily rank among the best in Southern India to date. Pattadakal Pattadakal Long before Pattadakal became an iconic site for temple design, this place served as the sacred ground where Chalukyan kings were crowned. The site also holds a special moment in design history, bringing together North Indian Nagara and South Indian Dravida architectural styles side by side, especially at the grand Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples, famous for their detailed wall carvings depicting scenes from Indian epics. The Hoysala temple in Belur. Belur Belur is home to the 12th-century Chennakeshava Temple, a soapstone masterwork built over the course of 100 years during the Hoysala period. The site sits on a unique star-shaped foundation decorated with animals and folklore depictions, and scenes from Indian epics. The temple complex is celebrated, above all, for its finely detailed Madanika dancer sculptures. Halebidu Halebidu The ruined Hoysala city of Halebidu ('Old City') tells a dramatic story: 14th-century invasions forced the empire to abandon the site, leaving its grand monuments frozen in time. An exterior view of the Rangeen Mahal in Bidar. Bidar Up on Karnataka's northern plateau, Bidar holds a rich history with a strong Persian and Islamic heritage from the Deccan Sultanate era. Built from local red laterite, the vast Bidar Fort complex encloses old royal quarters, ruined mosques, and traditional Turkish bathhouses. Outside the fort, the town is best known for the grand Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, the Bahmani Tombs at Ashtur, and its famous local Bidriware metalwork. Bijapur Mosque (Jumma Masjid), Vijayapura. Vijayapura (Bijapur) Walking around Vijayapura feels like stepping back into the height of the Adil Shahi Sultanate. The standout sight is Gol Gumbaz, home to one of the world's largest unsupported domes and a gallery that amplifies the quietest sounds. Elsewhere in town, you will spot the intricate, carved surfaces of the Ibrahim Rauza complex and the enormous Malik-e-Maidan cannon still resting on the ancient city ramparts. Kodagu The Western Ghats Chikkamagaluru and Kodagu aren't about ancient temples or historic ruins. They're all about cool mountain air and endless coffee estates. If you love trekking, Chikkamagaluru is the obvious choice, thanks to the trails up Mullayanagiri and the green slopes of Kudremukh. Down in Kodagu, things slow down a bit as it is mostly about spending time outdoors, wandering through spice gardens and taking easy trips to forest waterfalls like Abbey Falls and Iruppu Falls. Further north in Shivamogga, Jog Falls delivers pure dramatic scale, where the Sharavati river plunges down a rocky gorge surrounded by thick forest. Murudeshwar in Uttara Kannada district. Coastal Karnataka Located along Karnataka’s Arabian Sea coastline, Gokarna and Murudeshwar combine pilgrimage heritage with beach landscapes. In Gokarna, you can hike along the cliffs between beaches like Kudle and Om Beach. Murudeshwar is famous for its massive 123-foot Shiva statue that sits right at the edge of the ocean beside the main temple complex. St Mary's Island, Udupi Udupi Udupi is famous for its iconic Krishna temple, vegetarian dishes and easy access to the coast. Just a short boat ride from Malpe Beach, St Mary’s Island features striking hexagonal basalt columns formed by prehistoric volcanic activity.

articles.title: Through a freezing Srinagar night, young job aspirants demand a fair chance
articles.summary: Srinagar: As temperatures dipped in Srinagar on Saturday night, a group of young job aspirants remained at SK Park, determined to continue their sit-in against alleged irregularities in government recruitment examinations. Sitting under the open sky, the protesters vowed to continue their agitation indefinitely, demanding accountability for alleged examination fraud and changes to the recruitment system. The protest drew former Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah, who joined the students and spent the night at the site. Ruhullah recently resigned from the National Conference and his Lok Sabha seat after a prolonged rift with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah over the reservation policy, employment promises and the party’s position on Article 370. He said he was joining the students rather than leading their agitation. Kashmir feels the winter chill as Srinagar records season’s first sub-zero temperature As the night grew colder, Ruhullah alleged that police were preventing food and blankets from reaching the protesters. His office later claimed that police forcibly removed him and the students from the site. The immediate trigger for the agitation is an alleged cheating network uncovered during the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) recruitment examination conducted by the J&K Services Selection Board (JKSSB) on November 15 for 600 posts. Police have arrested 14 people, registered three FIRs and constituted a Special Investigation Team to investigate the suspected network, which allegedly involved electronic devices to facilitate cheating. The JKSSB, however, has maintained that the examination was not compromised. The recruitment agency has described the incident as an isolated attempt to use unfair means that was foiled by police intervention. The protesters are demanding an overhaul of the JKSSB, an independent investigation into the alleged examination racket. They also seek cancellation of examinations found to have been compromised by malpractice. They have also sought suspension of upcoming JKSSB examinations until the investigation is completed and corrective measures introduced. Another major demand is publication of the report of the government-appointed subcommittee reviewing the reservation policy, which aspirants say has remained pending for nearly two years. They have also sought action against officials and others found responsible for recruitment irregularities. The latest agitation has revived memories of earlier recruitment controversies. In 2022, examinations for 972 Finance Accounts Assistant and 163 Junior Engineer (Civil) posts were cancelled amid allegations of irregularities. The Police Sub-Inspector recruitment examination was also scrapped following allegations of a paper leak. More recently, 103 Fire and Emergency Services employees were terminated in December 2025 following an inquiry into alleged fraudulent appointments. Government employment remains a major aspiration in J&K, where large numbers of educated young people compete for limited public-sector vacancies. The repeated controversies have added to uncertainty among candidates who spend years preparing for competitive examinations. At Sher-e-Kashmir Park, the students remained firm on their demands, seeking transparency in recruitment and accountability for those found involved in malpractice

articles.title: 'Skills will command greater respect than certificates': PM Modi on AI
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said no one can take the livelihood of a person with skills amid increasing discussion about artificial intelligence. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan on Saturday, the prime minister added that invaders destroyed India's traditional skill infrastructure and targeted traditional craftsmanship, with the British later introducing an education system focused on producing clerks. Modi said that the times are changing and that India is moving towards becoming the world's skill capital. "When invaders came to India, their first attack was on our skills. They knew that the craftsmanship of Indians was making the country great and prosperous, and sought to destroy it by cutting off the thumbs of artisans," Modi told the gathering. Invaders cut thumbs of our craftsmen, damaged India’s traditional skill infra: PM Modi "The British were more sophisticated. They changed their methods. (British politician Thomas Babington) Macaulay imposed an education system that reduced our skill-based system to producing clerks," he said. Modi said that skill development and traditional craftsmanship took a back seat even after independence, with the emphasis continuing on clerical jobs. "Over time, being a paper clerk came to be seen as a matter of prestige," he added. Modi said the British used the education system to weaken India's traditional skill-based system and promote manufacturing in their country using Indian resources. "India has always been a country that respects skills. Look at the chikankari work here in Lucknow. For a long time, India's identity in the world was built around such skills. From fine muslin, Banarasi and Kanchipuram silk, Kashmiri pashmina and cotton textiles to kalamkari, and from steel used to make some of the world's finest swords to bronze and panchdhatu (five-metal alloy) sculptures, there were countless such crafts," he said. Talking about the possibility of artificial intelligence taking over jobs, Modi said, "There is a lot of discussion about AI, but remember that no one can take away the livelihood of a person who possesses skills." "Times are changing. Skilled individuals will command greater respect than those who merely hold certificates," he said. Further, Modi praised the people of the country for heeding his call to not buy gold. "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens to not buy gold if they don't need it. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell," he said. "I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji's request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation," he said. "Today, I'm going to say something else. Mark my words: Times are changing and people with skills will be valued more than those who go around with paper certificates, wearing suits and ties. Demand for those with skills, those with talent, will increase," he added. Modi said India can develop in the 21st century only by giving respect to skilled workers, adding that the government has taken several steps under the 'Shramev Jayate' initiative and established a separate Ministry of Skill Development. Emphasising the need for a change in society's perception of vocational education, Modi said Industrial Training Institute (ITI) graduates play a crucial role in running large companies. "Just as IIT students are respected, my ITI students should receive the same respect. Even the biggest companies may have two or three people carrying paper certificates, but they need 200 to 300 ITI-trained people to provide strength and run the company," he said. Karnataka aims to skill 30 lakh youth in seven years with Rs 5,000 crore outlay: D K Shivakumar "Be it IIT or ITI, for me, students are the treasure, strength and future of the country," he said. Recalling the COVID-19 pandemic, Modi said the exodus of workers from cities to villages highlighted the importance of skilled manpower in sustaining everyday life. "People realised that no matter how wealthy one is, it is impossible to lead a normal life without skilled manpower. These skilled workers are the ones who kept things running and sustained the nation," he said. Acquiring skills is not merely about working on machines, but also about making people's lives easier and enhancing the country's capabilities, the prime minister told the youngsters. "There was a time when India used to import mobile phones. Today, the daughters of our country are manufacturing them. Mobile phones made in India are now being exported across the globe. It is because of you that the country's manufacturing capacity is growing. This is why ITIs are being given such great importance today," he said. CBSE scheme for 2028: 5 compulsory subjects, optional skill paper as safety net in Class 10 exams Nearly 5,000 new ITIs have been built in a decade, Modi said. "The number of those studying in ITIs has also increased by over 5 lakh, with the number of girls increasing more than two and a half times," he said. Modi said Uttar Pradesh's expanding infrastructure and industrial base are creating new opportunities for young people. He said large mobile manufacturing facilities are coming up in the state and a semiconductor manufacturing facility is also being established. He also referred to the production of BrahMos missiles in Uttar Pradesh. Modi also announced that India will host the 2027 WorldSkills Competition in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Modi lauded the Yogi Adityanath government for creating a safe environment for women in the state. He recalled that a woman told him during a factory inauguration in Varanasi, his parliamentary constituency, that she could return home safely even after working until 11 pm. "This is not an ordinary thing. Under the leadership of Yogi ji, the BJP government has created an environment of security in Uttar Pradesh," he said. "Security and confidence in prosperity will build a developed India. I tell every young person in the country that the entire sky is open before you. Dream big, develop your skills and work with all your strength to fulfil your dreams. Never feel that you are alone. Whenever you feel so, remember that I stand with you," the PM said. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary and senior state BJP leaders attended the event. articles.title: Selections of teachers without statutory conformity invalid: Supreme Court
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has ruled that appointments of teachers for classes governed by the Right to Education Act must strictly conform to statutory qualifications, holding that selections made contrary to the National Council for Teacher Education Act are invalid and liable to be set aside. A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi dismissed special leave petitions related to the selection of 10,323 teachers in Tripura, which were previously cancelled by the high court and the Supreme Court. The appointments, made pursuant to advertisements issued in 2002, 2006 and 2009, had been set aside by the Tripura High Court in Tanmoy Nath and Others Vs State of Tripura (2014) for being arbitrary, illegal and contrary to the NCTE Act and relevant policies. The high court’s decision attained finality after the Supreme Court disposed of challenges to it on March 29, 2017. Supreme Court dismisses plea seeking directions concerning restoration and functioning of Shenbagavalli weir That order directed a fresh selection process to be completed by December 31, 2017, while allowing the existing teachers to continue in the interim. It also stipulated that qualifications for teachers covered by the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, must conform to the statute. The continuance was later extended up to March 31, 2020, after which termination orders were issued. Challenging the terminations, the teachers argued that the Tanmoy Nath judgment could not bind them in the absence of individual notices and that long service of over a decade protected them. The State maintained that the high court decision operated in rem against all appointees under the impugned advertisements. The Supreme Court agreed with the State. “It is clear from the order of this court dated 29.03.2017 that the candidates who had participated in the selection process pursuant to the advertisements in question, whether selected or not, were to be allowed to participate in the fresh selection process by relaxing their age but subject to their having necessary qualifications,” the bench noted. It further observed no doubt fresh recruitment exercise could not be completed by or before the date, but this period has been extended from time to time and all those who were appointed were allowed to continue up to March 31, 2020. "In such circumstances, if the services have been terminated in compliance of the earlier order passed in Tanmoy Nath which has been affirmed by this Court, no fault can be found with such orders. In our view, the writ petitions were rightly dismissed,” the bench said. The court rejected contentions that the earlier ruling did not cover already appointed teachers or all categories of teachers, finding the entire selection under the advertisements annulled.

India is hosting the three-day civilisational summit at the historic precinct of the Purana Qila, which was inaugurated on Friday evening by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the presence of various SCO delegates, including Malik from Pakistan . "This (Purana) Qila, where we are sitting, is in itself a story. A fort, whose foundation was laid by Humayun, who had a descent from the Timurid (dynasty) linkage.. came from Central Asia. And, Sher Shah Suri further built on it, who was an Afghan. One wall, two rivals, meaning two rulers and one fort, meaning two layers and one trench," the Pakistan minister said. India and Bulgaria discuss bilateral ties, IMEC, Black Sea situation Malik's office posted a video of his remarks on X and also wrote in Urdu that this Qila is a "story". Humayun was the second Mughal emperor, whose final resting place -- the famed Humayun's Tomb -- a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Nizamuddin area is located not far from the Purana Qila. The tomb is the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent and marked a major departure from earlier funerary traditions. It is a pioneering example of Indo-Islamic architecture and a proud representation of India’s heritage, according to the website of the culture ministry. Amid unease in India-Pakistan ties since the 2025 Pahalgam attack, the minister is visiting India for the first time. Purana Qila reflects India’s shared cultural heritage, says Pakistan minister In his remarks delivered at the thematic session 'Civilisational and Cultural Expressions', chaired by Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, he also said, "dialogue is between distinct identities, and between diversity, and we have come here for that dialogue only". "Meaning, many voices, many identities, and their dialogues, and free flow of ideas, among them... free flow of identities. The wisdom lies in it, the wisdom lies in embracing it, embellishing it. So, wisdom is there in it, and needs courage too. And, we have gathered here to celebrate these two things," Malik said, without elaborating. India is hosting the SCO forum at the Purana Qila -- a centrally protected monument in the heart of Delhi -- to showcase the richness of its civilisational wealth and the multiple layers of history spanning thousands of years. As part of the Forum, a special site exhibition, titled 'Astitva -- The Essence of our Existence', offers SCO delegates an immersive account of Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1,200 BC to 1200 CE, including excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries. SCO engagement should pave way for bilateral talks between India, Pakistan: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq Shekhawat, in his address said, “Shared cultural heritage is a strong bridge connecting SCO nations" and asserted that historical connections have played a significant role in bringing countries closer to one another. They have also effectively highlighted the immense potential of cultural cooperation in fostering mutual understanding, trust, and friendship, the Union culture minister said. "Our civilisations are not merely legacies of the past, but living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate our present and inspire future generations," Shekhawat said. "And, the way Shekhawat sahab, you cited the examples of the layers, which have existed here for thousands of years," Malik said, referring to the archaeological evidences at the Qila site. articles.summary: Ranchi: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has urged Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium to urgently recommend a successor to High Court Chief Justice M S Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27. In a letter to the CJI and judges of the Collegium, Soren said prolonged interim arrangements could create uncertainty within the judicial establishment. The CM said frequent transitions disrupt administrative continuity and institutional planning in the high court. Soren also sought a stable judicial leadership in the Jharkhand High Court to maintain public confidence in the justice delivery system. “Without the Collegium's immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangement… I hope it (the Collegium) will not disagree with me that the office of the Chief Justice is central to the administrative and judicial functioning of a high court,” he said in the letter. Supreme Court collegium recommends four judges for appointment as High Court Chief Justices “… As the head of the state government, I am compelled to draw your attention to the fact that an incoming Chief Justice has not been designated nor has any Hon’ble Justice been transferred to the Jharkhand High Court in advance… on the superannuation of Hon'ble Chief Justice M S Sonak on November 27, 2026,” Soren said. Prior to the appointment of the incumbent Chief Justice on January 9, the high court has been “adorned by four Chief Justices since the superannuation of Justice Ravi Ranjan on December 19, 2022… one of His Lordships having a term of a fortnight”, the chief minister said in his letter to the CJI. “During this period, Acting Chief Justices have been appointed on three occasions for terms ranging from two months to six months. I must, in my own humble way, express utmost respect and admiration for the foresight and dedication shown by the Collegium earlier this year to strengthen institutional continuity and judicial administration in its Statement of February 26, 2026,” he said. Soren cited the Collegium’s decision that to strengthen the efficiency and quality of administration of justice, a judge proposed to take over the high court as its Chief Justice may be transferred well in advance, preferably two months before the vacancy arises, so that the recommendee becomes well conversant with the high court's affairs. “The Collegium will appreciate that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment,” he added.

articles.title: UoH students launch protest seeking professor’s termination over casteist remarks
articles.summary: University of Hyderabad students have launched an indefinite protest demanding the termination of Dr Vijaya Ramdas Mandala, a faculty member in the History Department, over his alleged derogatory remarks about Dalit students in an email exchange. The remarks were allegedly made after a former student expressed hesitation regarding incorporating certain suggestions made by Vijaya Ramdas into his research because of ethical concerns. The incident took place in April but came to light only recently. The protest has been called by the Students’ Union, which comprises various student groups, including the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the Ambedkar Students’ Association, the Dalit Students’ Union,and the Tribal Students’ Forum. Students have been staging a sit-in outside the Social Sciences building, demanding Vijaya Ramdas’s termination. “We will not call off the protest until Vijaya Ramdas is terminated,” PhD student Aditya Rao told TNM. “We had protested earlier too, but no concrete action was taken against him,” he added. The screenshots of an email exchange were shown to TNM by student activists. Through the emails, Vijaya Ramdas contacted Sandeep (name changed), who is a PhD student at Manchester Business School, about corrections to his chapter for a forthcoming book by Bloomsbury India. In the email thread, the History professor refers to former students from the Dalit community as “untouchables” more than once. He also refers to another student studying at Nottingham as “Dalit untouchable idiot”. The email exchange, which took place between April 14 and 16, grew increasingly tense after Sandeep said he would need the permission of his current university to anonymise the people he was being asked to name in the research, to avoid being flagged for ethical violations. “It will take months to get an ethical review committee's decision from the University of Manchester to write the names asked for in my chapter and publish it as a PhD student of the University,” Sandeep said. Vijaya Ramdas responded: “At Indian business schools, or even at Harvard Business School or Rotman Business School, your chapter discussing managerial and business people would not have been a problem. It's not a History Department perspective, as 99.5% of History departments worldwide do not deal with business history.” Sandeep then pointed to another obstacle in the research, saying that one of the students who is part of his research would need approval to conduct research in India. He also said the researcher was unclear about the archival sources. Vijaya Ramdas responded: “The recent German PhD who comes from an untouchable Dalit background also said to me the same thing about his collection of archives in India.” He further wrote: “A large chunk of the Indian population is from non-Aryan and non-wealthy backgrounds, including backward states like Bihar and Jharkhand, which resemble some countries in Africa on the political map of India and across the globe. This also happened to another Dalit untouchable idiot at Nottingham, who is working part-time in a hotel in England after his post-UK PhD (sic).” Vijaya Ramdas also called Sandeep “anti-Indian”, threatened to withhold academic support, and said his chapter would not be included in the book. He said people from poverty-ridden backgrounds developed “Pakistani-centric thinking (not knowing that one cannot emulate class, one should be born in a high class and culture) in a country known as Mini-Pakistan.” “I am terminating further communication with you, but also will not provide academic support from third-rate, poverty-ridden idiots from Bihar and Jharkhand henceforth,” he concluded. In addition to seeking Vijaya Ramdas’s termination, the students have called for his arrest under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. They have also demanded that Bloomsbury India suspend its ongoing project with him and that caste sensitisation workshops be held across the University. TNM reached out to Vijaya Ramdas for his comments, but received no response.
